author: w. t. hanley
title: Judy Chu introduces bipartisan bill for foster youth education access
text:
Judy Chu, U.S. Congresswoman representing California’s 28th district since 2009, announced the introduction of new bipartisan legislation aimed at supporting foster youth in higher education through her Twitter account on February 11, 2026.
In a post published that day, Chu stated, “Yesterday, I introduced the bipartisan Foster Youth Postsecondary Education Access and Success Act with @RepNateMoran to strengthen and modernize Education & Training Vouchers (ETVs) for foster and transition-age youth. https://t.co/bIGbKQ2r7P”.
She followed up by emphasizing the challenges faced by foster youth in accessing educational support: “@RepNateMoran ETVs help foster youth afford college, but the amount is too low and only about 1/3 of eligible students actually receive support. By increasing the value of the vouchers and addressing barriers to access, this bill will help ensure more foster youth can earn a degree and pursue”.
Later that morning, Chu addressed actions taken by former President Donald Trump regarding congressional members: “Donald Trump tried to throw Members of Congress in jail for reminding servicemembers they don’t have to follow illegal orders. That is an outrageous abuse of power. He is weaponizing DOJ to silence dissent and not one Republican has stepped up to stop him.”
Chu has represented California’s 28th District since replacing Hilda Solis in 2009. Before her tenure in Congress, she served in the California State Assembly from 2001 to 2006. Born in Los Angeles in 1953 and currently residing in Monterey Park, Chu graduated from UCLA with a BA in 1974.
